expectation: intentRequest rebuilds the request from a fixed list of invoice fields that leaves out issuedAt, so newIntent, which computes the fee with lateFee(prepared.total, prepared.issuedAt, at), gets a due instant of NaN and an intent created while its invoice is late has a fee of 0 and an amount equal to the total.
finding:
- `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:8-10,13,19`, `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:13-15`, `src/platform/invoice-terms.mjs:4-8`: `createPaymentIntent` drops `invoice.issuedAt` before constructing the payment intent, causing late invoices to receive a `0` late fee.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:179,267`): "A payment request's invoice is due 20160 minutes after its `issuedAt` and is late when `now()` is equal to or later than that instant." and "An intent created while its invoice is late has a `fee` of 5 percent of `total`, rounded down to a whole unit; otherwise its `fee` is 0. Its `amount` is `total` plus `fee`."
  - Implementation evidence: `intentRequest` in `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:8-10` destructures `{requestKey, invoice: {id, memberId, total}}` and returns `{requestKey, invoiceId: id, memberId, total}`, omitting `issuedAt`. `createPaymentIntent` (`src/payments/payment-service.mjs:13,19`) passes that object as `prepared` to `newIntent` (`src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:13-15`), which calls `lateFee(prepared.total, prepared.issuedAt, at)` (`src/platform/invoice-terms.mjs:4-8`).
  - Impact: Because `prepared.issuedAt` is `undefined`, `dueAt(undefined)` evaluates to `NaN` and `isLate(undefined, at)` (`at >= NaN`) is always `false`, so intents created at or after `issuedAt + 20160 minutes` always get `fee: 0` and `amount: total` instead of the 5% late fee.
  - Fix: Include `issuedAt` in `intentRequest` in `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:8-10` (`const intentRequest = ({requestKey, invoice: {id, issuedAt, memberId, total}}) => ({requestKey, invoiceId: id, issuedAt, memberId, total});`).

expectation: hasEnded compares minutesBetween(at, endAt), whole minutes truncated toward zero, with 0, so a closure with less than one minute left (for example 30 seconds) counts as ended: adding it is rejected and it is left out of the upcoming closures.
finding:
- `src/schedules/closures.mjs:26`, `src/platform/time.mjs:9`, `src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs:31,56`: `hasEnded` truncates `(closure.endAt - at) / MINUTE` toward zero, treating closures that end less than one full minute after `now()` as already ended.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:184,189`): "A closure whose `endAt` is not later than `now()` is rejected." and "Upcoming desk closures are the building's active closures whose `endAt` is later than `now()`, by ascending `startAt`, then `id`."
  - Implementation evidence: `hasEnded` in `src/schedules/closures.mjs:26` evaluates `minutesBetween(at, closure.endAt) <= 0`, where `minutesBetween` (`src/platform/time.mjs:9`) computes `Math.trunc((to - from) / MINUTE)`. `addClosure` (`src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs:31`) rejects when `hasEnded(prepared, at)` is true, and `upcomingClosures` (`src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs:56`) keeps only closures with `!hasEnded(closure, at)`.
  - Impact: Whenever `0 < closure.endAt - at < 60_000` (for example, `at = 1_000` and `closure.endAt = 30_000`), `closure.endAt` is strictly later than `now()`, yet `Math.trunc(29_000 / 60_000)` is `0 <= 0`, so `addClosure` wrongly rejects the closure and `upcomingClosures` omits the active closure.
  - Fix: Define `export const hasEnded = (closure, at) => closure.endAt <= at;` in `src/schedules/closures.mjs:26`.

expectation: The single withdraw rule for waiting and offered entries carries the 60-minute cutoff, so a waiting entry whose startAt is less than 60 minutes from now cannot be withdrawn, although the limit applies only to offered entries.
finding:
- `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:58-64`, `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,19-26`, `src/waitlist/queue.mjs:9,13`: `acceptOffer` transitions the entry to `accepted` before checking `isLapsing`, causing expired offers to be accepted instead of rejected.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:50,182`): "Only a nonexpired `offered` entry may be accepted; acceptance sets `accepted` and `acceptedAt` and books nothing." and "A waitlist offer is expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`."
  - Implementation evidence: `acceptOffer` (`src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`) first computes `const next = moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at);` (`src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,24`), which returns an object with `state: 'accepted'`, and only afterward checks `if (isLapsing(next, at))`. `isLapsing` (`src/waitlist/queue.mjs:13`) checks `entry.state === 'offered' && isExpired(entry, at)`.
  - Impact: Because `next.state` is `'accepted'`, `isLapsing(next, at)` always evaluates to `false`, so calling `acceptOffer` when `now() >= entry.expiresAt` succeeds and saves the expired offer as `accepted` instead of rejecting it.
  - Fix: Check `if (isLapsing(entry, at))` (or check `isExpired(entry, at)` after verifying `entry.state === 'offered'`) on the input `entry` before calling `moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at)` in `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`.

expectation: The single withdraw rule for waiting and offered entries carries the 60-minute cutoff, so a waiting entry whose startAt is less than 60 minutes from now cannot be withdrawn, although the limit applies only to offered entries.
finding:
- `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:9,22`, `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:66-71`: `moveEntry` applies the 60-minute `startAt` withdrawal cutoff to `waiting` waitlist entries even though only `offered` entries have that limit.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:51,183`): "Only a `waiting` or `offered` entry may be withdrawn, setting `withdrawn` and `withdrawnAt`; withdrawing a `withdrawn` entry returns it with no persistence." and "Withdrawing an `offered` waitlist entry is rejected when its `startAt` is less than 60 minutes after `now()`. A `waiting` entry has no such limit."
  - Implementation evidence: In `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:9`, a single transition rule `{action: 'withdraw', from: ['waiting', 'offered'], to: 'withdrawn', stamp: 'withdrawnAt', cutoff: WITHDRAW_CUTOFF_MINUTES}` covers both `'waiting'` and `'offered'`, and line 22 throws whenever `rule.cutoff !== undefined && entry.startAt - at < minutes(rule.cutoff)`. `withdrawEntry` (`src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:67`) delegates directly to `moveEntry(entry, 'withdraw', now())`.
  - Impact: Calling `withdrawEntry` on a `waiting` entry whose `startAt` is less than 60 minutes after `now()` (for example, 30 minutes before `startAt`) throws `too late to withdraw` instead of marking and saving the entry as `withdrawn`.
  - Fix: Split the withdrawal transition in `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:9` into `{action: 'withdraw', from: ['waiting'], to: 'withdrawn', stamp: 'withdrawnAt'}` (without `cutoff`) and `{action: 'withdraw', from: ['offered'], to: 'withdrawn', stamp: 'withdrawnAt', cutoff: WITHDRAW_CUTOFF_MINUTES}`.

expectation: ENTRY_DEFAULTS gives active: true and prepareRoom spreads it under the room entry, so a room entry without an active value becomes active and is selected for the report, although only rooms whose active value is true may be.
finding:
- `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7,9-16,36`, `src/utilization/utilization-service.mjs:40,62`: `prepareRoom` defaults a missing `active` field on room entries to `true`, selecting rooms whose supplied `active` value is not `true`.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:149`): "A utilization report's requested amenities are lowercased and deduplicated, room amenities are lowercased, and only rooms whose `active` value is `true` and that contain every requested amenity are selected."
  - Implementation evidence: `ENTRY_DEFAULTS` in `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7` is `Object.freeze({active: true, amenities: []})`, and `prepareRoom` (`src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:10,15`) merges `const room = {...ENTRY_DEFAULTS, ...entry};` before `loadDirectory` filters with `room.active === true` on line 36. `buildReport` and `generateUtilizationReport` (`src/utilization/utilization-service.mjs:40,62`) load rooms through `loadDirectory`.
  - Impact: When a supplied room entry omits `active` (for example, `{id: 'r1', buildingId: 'b1', capacity: 4, amenities: []}`), its `active` value is `undefined` rather than `true`, yet `ENTRY_DEFAULTS` sets `room.active` to `true` and includes the room in the utilization report's room and building rows.
  - Fix: Remove `active: true` from `ENTRY_DEFAULTS` in `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7` (`const ENTRY_DEFAULTS = Object.freeze({amenities: []});`) so only room entries whose supplied `active` property is strictly `true` are selected.

expectation: A credit reason is trimmed instead of being stored exactly as supplied.
finding:
- `src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:9-13`, `src/billing/invoice-service.mjs:16,21,30,40`: `prepareCredit` trims each credit's `reason` before storing instead of preserving the supplied string verbatim.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:135`): "Its `credits` must be a list; each credit's `amount` must be a non-negative integer and its `reason` must not be blank after trimming; the reason is stored exactly as supplied."
  - Implementation evidence: `prepareCredit` in `src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:11-12` validates `if (!trimmed(credit.reason))` and then returns `Object.freeze({amount: credit.amount, reason: credit.reason.trim()})`. `prepareInvoiceRequest` (`src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:30`) maps `request.credits` through `prepareCredit`, and `draftFor` (`src/billing/invoice-service.mjs:16`) copies `prepared.credits` into previews (`previewInvoice`, line 21) and stored invoices (`issueInvoice`, lines 30 and 40).
  - Impact: Supplying a credit with leading or trailing whitespace in `reason`, such as `'  service outage  '`, strips the surrounding whitespace and stores `'service outage'` instead of the exact supplied value.
  - Fix: Return `Object.freeze({amount: credit.amount, reason: credit.reason})` in `prepareCredit` (`src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:12`) after verifying `trimmed(credit.reason)` is non-empty.

expectation: newIntent passes PAYMENT_TERMS.authorizationHold, which is already minutes(10080) in milliseconds, to addMinutes, which multiplies by a minute again, so a new authorization expires 604,800,000 minutes later instead of 10080 minutes: an old authorization keeps blocking new intents for its invoice and can still be captured long after it should have expired.
finding:
- `src/platform/site-settings.mjs:11`, `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:7-11,25,32-35`, `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:18-20,30`, `src/platform/time.mjs:7`: New payment intents convert `PAYMENT_TERMS.authorizationHold` from minutes to milliseconds twice, setting `expiresAt` 60,000 times too far in the future.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:114,186`): "A new payment intent's `id` comes from `nextId()`; it is `authorized` with `authorizedAt` from `now()`, a hold `expiresAt` 10080 minutes later, `captured` and `refunded` of 0, and a `lastRefund` of null." and "A payment authorization is expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`; expiry never changes `state`. Only a nonexpired `authorized` intent may be captured."
  - Implementation evidence: `PAYMENT_TERMS.authorizationHold` in `src/platform/site-settings.mjs:11` is already `minutes(10_080)` (`604_800_000` ms), and `newIntent` in `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:25` computes `expiresAt: addMinutes(at, PAYMENT_TERMS.authorizationHold)`, where `addMinutes` (`src/platform/time.mjs:7`) multiplies its second argument by `MINUTE` (`60_000`) again.
  - Impact: Every created payment intent stores and publishes `expiresAt = at + 36_288_000_000_000` instead of `at + 604_800_000`; an `authorized` intent older than 10,080 minutes is not treated as expired by `capturePayment` or `blocksNewIntent` in `createPaymentIntent`.
  - Fix: Either store `authorizationHoldMinutes: 10_080` in `PAYMENT_TERMS` or compute `expiresAt: at + PAYMENT_TERMS.authorizationHold` in `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:25`.

expectation: paymentStatus passes the invoice record current to netPaid as its invoiceId argument; netPaid compares each intent's invoiceId (a string) with it using ===, and a string never equals an object, so no intent matches and the status reports paid 0 even after an intent of the invoice was captured.
finding:
- `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:47-56`, `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:53-55`: `paymentStatus` passes the `current` invoice object instead of the normalized `invoiceId` string to `netPaid`, causing `paid` to always be `0`.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:179`): "A payment status reports `dueAt`, `late` and `paid`, the sum of `captured` minus `refunded` over its `captured` and `refunded` intents."
  - Implementation evidence: In `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:49,54`, `paymentStatus` builds `const current = {...invoice, id: requireInvoiceId(invoice.id)};` and computes `paid: netPaid(await store.list(), current)`. `netPaid` (`src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:53-55`) filters intents with `intent.invoiceId === invoiceId`.
  - Impact: Comparing the string `intent.invoiceId` with the object `current` via `===` is always `false`, so `paymentStatus` reports `paid: 0` even when captured or partially refunded intents exist for that invoice.
  - Fix: Pass `current.id` to `netPaid` in `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:54` (`paid: netPaid(await store.list(), current.id)`).

expectation: AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow is minutes(10080), a number of milliseconds, but prepareQuery compares it with windowSpan(query), which counts minutes ((until - from) / MINUTE), so the 10080-minute limit never triggers and longer query windows are accepted.
finding:
- `src/audit/retention.mjs:5,13`, `src/audit/audit-query.mjs:9`, `src/audit/audit-service.mjs:42-50`: Audit query validation compares a window length in minutes against a limit expressed in milliseconds, failing to reject query windows longer than 10080 minutes.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:97,146`): "An audit query has integer `from` and `until`, `until` later than `from` by at most 10080 minutes, and a `limit` that is an integer from 1 to 500, or 500 when absent (undefined or null)." and "An actor summary takes a query that is valid under the audit query rules, `limit` included, and counts every entry it matches, ignoring `limit`, as `{actor, entries}` by descending count, then ascending `actor`."
  - Implementation evidence: `AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow` in `src/audit/retention.mjs:5` is `minutes(10_080)` (`604_800_000` ms), whereas `windowSpan` in `src/audit/retention.mjs:13` computes `(window.until - window.from) / MINUTE` (in minutes). `prepareQuery` in `src/audit/audit-query.mjs:9` checks `if (windowSpan(query) > AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow)`, which is used by `queryEntries` and `actorSummary` (`src/audit/audit-service.mjs:42-50`).
  - Impact: Any query with `until - from` above 10,080 minutes and up to 604,800,000 minutes (for example, a 20,000-minute window where `until - from === 1_200_000_000`) passes `prepareQuery` instead of being rejected.
  - Fix: Use consistent units, either setting `maxQueryWindow: 10_080` in minutes or comparing `(query.until - query.from) > AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow` directly in milliseconds.

expectation: releaseTime rounds now() up to a whole minute with minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1) and then adds wait, but wait is counted from the local minute of day, which localMinuteOfDay takes from the start of the current minute; when now() is not on a minute boundary the result is one minute late (22:59:30 local with endMinute 23:00 gives 23:01 instead of 23:00), so releaseAt is not the first minute boundary after now() whose local minute is endMinute.
finding:
- `src/messaging/quiet-hours.mjs:16,18-21,32-36`, `src/messaging/messaging-service.mjs:49`: `releaseTime` adds `minutes(wait)` to a rounded-up minute boundary while computing `wait` from a rounded-down minute boundary, shifting `releaseAt` one minute too late whenever `now()` is not on an exact minute boundary.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:206`): "A message created in quiet hours is saved as `queued` with `queuedAt` from `now()`, `releaseAt` at the first minute boundary after `now()` whose local minute is `endMinute`; it is not sent."
  - Implementation evidence: In `src/messaging/quiet-hours.mjs:32-36`, `releaseTime` computes `const minute = localMinuteOfDay(at, hours.offset);` (which floors `at` via `minuteStart(at)` on lines 16 and 19) and `const wait = (hours.quiet.endMinute - minute + DAY_MINUTES) % DAY_MINUTES;`, then returns `minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1) + minutes(wait)`. `sendMessage` (`src/messaging/messaging-service.mjs:49`) stores this value as `releaseAt`.
  - Impact: During quiet hours `minute !== endMinute`, so `wait >= 1`. For any `at` not already divisible by `60_000` (for example, `at = 570_000` at `00:09:30` UTC with `offset = 0`, `startMinute = 0`, `endMinute = 10`), `minute` is `9` and `wait` is `1`, while `minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1)` rounds up to `600_000` (`00:10:00`), yielding `releaseAt = 660_000` (`00:11:00`, local minute `11`) instead of `600_000` (`00:10:00`, local minute `10`).
  - Fix: Return `minuteStart(at) + minutes(wait)` in `src/messaging/quiet-hours.mjs:35` (since `wait` is in `1..1439` whenever `isQuiet(hours, at)` is true, `minuteStart(at) + minutes(wait)` is strictly greater than `at` and lands on local minute `endMinute`).

expectation: formatList writes each item through formatText, so a list item that starts with =, +, - or @ gets the ' prefix (for example the list ['-a', 'b'] is written '-a;b), although only text values get that prefix and a list's items are written as stored.
finding:
- `src/exports/value-format.mjs:5,7-10,27-30`, `src/exports/reservation-columns.mjs:29`, `src/exports/export-service.mjs:9,13`: `formatList` applies `text` formula-prefix escaping to individual list items instead of writing list items as stored.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:242-243`): "A `text` value must be a string and is written as stored, but with `'` prefixed when it starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`." and "a `list` of strings is joined with `;`, its items written as stored."
  - Implementation evidence: `formatList` in `src/exports/value-format.mjs:27-30` formats a `list` value via `value.map(formatText).join(';')`, where `formatText` (`src/exports/value-format.mjs:5,7-10`) prepends `'` whenever a string matches `/^[=+\-@]/`. `ROOM_COLUMNS` defines `amenities` as `kind: 'list'` (`src/exports/reservation-columns.mjs:29`), used by `exportRooms` (`src/exports/export-service.mjs:13`) and `exportRecords` (`src/exports/export-service.mjs:9`).
  - Impact: A `list` containing items starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` (for example, `['wifi', '+phone']` or `['-av']`) is written as `"wifi;'+phone"` or `"'-av"` with `'` injected before each matching item instead of writing the items as stored (`"wifi;+phone"` or `"-av"`).
  - Fix: Change `src/exports/value-format.mjs:29` from `return value.map(formatText).join(';');` to `return value.join(';');`.

expectation: hasAmenities compares the size of the union with room.amenities.length; after lowercasing, a room amenity list with duplicates (Whiteboard, whiteboard) has a union smaller than its length, so that room is never eligible even when it has every requested amenity.
finding:
- `src/reservations/catalog.mjs:5,16`, `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:12,18,28,31`: `hasAmenities` compares `Set` cardinality against `room.amenities.length` without deduplicating `room.amenities`, misclassifying rooms that list duplicate or case-variant amenity names.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:77`): "Amenity names are compared case-insensitively, and a room must contain every requested amenity."
  - Implementation evidence: `normalizeRoom` (`src/reservations/catalog.mjs:5`) lowercases `merged.amenities` via `.map((amenity) => amenity.toLowerCase())` without removing duplicates, and `hasAmenities` (`src/reservations/catalog.mjs:16`) evaluates `new Set([...room.amenities, ...amenities]).size === room.amenities.length`. Both `createReservation` (`src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:12,18`) and `listEligibleRooms` (`src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:28,31`) rely on `loadRooms` and `hasAmenities`.
  - Impact: If a room has duplicate normalized amenities such as `['wifi', 'WiFi']` (`room.amenities.length === 2`, unique size `1`), requesting `[]` or `['wifi']` produces `Set.size === 1 !== 2` and wrongly rejects an eligible room; conversely, requesting an absent amenity such as `['projector']` produces `new Set(['wifi', 'wifi', 'projector']).size === 2 === room.amenities.length` and wrongly treats the room as containing `'projector'`.
  - Fix: Check each requested amenity against a `Set` of the room's normalized amenities (for example, `const available = new Set(room.amenities); return amenities.every((amenity) => available.has(amenity));`, optionally also deduplicating in `normalizeRoom`).

finding:
- `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:58-64`, `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,19-26`, `src/waitlist/queue.mjs:9,13`: `acceptOffer` transitions the entry to `accepted` before checking `isLapsing`, causing expired offers to be accepted instead of rejected.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:50,182`): "Only a nonexpired `offered` entry may be accepted; acceptance sets `accepted` and `acceptedAt` and books nothing." and "A waitlist offer is expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`."
  - Implementation evidence: `acceptOffer` (`src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`) first computes `const next = moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at);` (`src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,24`), which returns an object with `state: 'accepted'`, and only afterward checks `if (isLapsing(next, at))`. `isLapsing` (`src/waitlist/queue.mjs:13`) checks `entry.state === 'offered' && isExpired(entry, at)`.
  - Impact: Because `next.state` is `'accepted'`, `isLapsing(next, at)` always evaluates to `false`, so calling `acceptOffer` when `now() >= entry.expiresAt` succeeds and saves the expired offer as `accepted` instead of rejecting it.
  - Fix: Check `if (isLapsing(entry, at))` (or check `isExpired(entry, at)` after verifying `entry.state === 'offered'`) on the input `entry` before calling `moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at)` in `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`.

expectation: applyTransition copies the record with a shallow spread and then pushes onto next.history, which is the same array as the received record's history, so confirm, cancel and reschedule modify the reservation object they receive.
finding:
- `src/reservations/transitions.mjs:16-17`, `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:37,45,58`: `applyTransition` mutates the input reservation's `history` array in place instead of leaving the received reservation unmodified.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:8`): "Operations never modify a reservation object they receive; they return new records."
  - Implementation evidence: `applyTransition` in `src/reservations/transitions.mjs:16-17` performs a shallow object spread (`const next = {...record, state: rule.to};`) and then executes `next.history.push({state: rule.to, at});`. `confirmReservation` (`src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:37`), `cancelReservation` (`src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:45`), and `rescheduleReservation` (`src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:58`) pass their input `reservation` directly into `applyTransition`.
  - Impact: Because `next.history` aliases `record.history`, confirming, canceling (from `held` or `confirmed`), or rescheduling a reservation mutates `reservation.history` on the caller's original object by appending the new transition entry to it.
  - Fix: Replace `next.history.push({state: rule.to, at})` in `src/reservations/transitions.mjs:16-17` with a new array copy, such as `const next = {...record, state: rule.to, history: [...record.history, {state: rule.to, at}]};`.

expectation: rescheduleReservation never applies the 240-minute duration limit to the snapped new window.
finding:
- `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:53-69`, `src/reservations/policy.mjs:5`: `rescheduleReservation` does not enforce the 240-minute maximum duration on the snapped reschedule window.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:21,197`): "A snapped window lasts at most 240 minutes." and "The new window must have an `endAt` value later than its `startAt` value. It is then snapped, and the snapped window must satisfy the duration limit and be available."
  - Implementation evidence: In `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:56-57`, `rescheduleReservation` computes `const window = {roomId: reservation.roomId, ...snapWindow({startAt, endAt})};` and checks `isRoomAvailable(...)`, then transitions, reprices, and saves the rescheduled hold without calling `exceedsMaxDuration(window)` (`src/reservations/policy.mjs:5`).
  - Impact: Calling `rescheduleReservation` with a new window whose snapped span exceeds 240 minutes (for example, 300 minutes) succeeds and persists an overlong reservation instead of rejecting the reschedule.
  - Fix: Check `if (exceedsMaxDuration(window)) throw new Error('reservation is too long');` in `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs` immediately after computing the snapped `window` and before mutating or saving state.

expectation: recordBadgeEvent looks up the event key through findKeyedEvent(store, prepared), which reads store.list(event); the event carries the event's buildingId, which the badge store (createAppendLog) destructures as a building filter, so a key already recorded for an event in another building is not found and the event is recorded again.
finding:
- `src/badges/badge-service.mjs:5-7,15-18`, `src/platform/append-log.mjs:6-8`: Badge `eventKey` idempotency lookup only searches the current event's building instead of all buildings.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:167`): "A badge event's `eventKey` is trimmed and lowercased; a non-string or blank key counts as absent. - `src/maintenance/ticket-service.mjs:66,70,82-88,102-104`, `src/maintenance/ticket-states.mjs:18`, `src/maintenance/ticket-policy.mjs:31-35,47`, `src/platform/records.mjs:1-5`: `clearPlannedWork` spreads `ticket` before `replan(ticket, null)`, leaving the previous `plannedWork` property on the saved ticket instead of clearing it.

finding:

finding:
- `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7,9-16,36`, `src/utilization/utilization-service.mjs:40,62`: `prepareRoom` defaults a missing `active` field on room entries to `true`, selecting rooms whose supplied `active` value is not `true`.

finding:
- `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:58-64`, `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,19-26`, `src/waitlist/queue.mjs:9,13`: `acceptOffer` transitions the entry to `accepted` before checking `isLapsing`, causing expired offers to be accepted instead of rejected.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:50,182`): "Only a nonexpired `offered` entry may be accepted; acceptance sets `accepted` and `acceptedAt` and books nothing." and "A waitlist offer is expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`."
  - Implementation evidence: `acceptOffer` (`src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`) first computes `const next = moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at);` (`src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,24`), which returns an object with `state: 'accepted'`, and only afterward checks `if (isLapsing(next, at))`. `isLapsing` (`src/waitlist/queue.mjs:13`) checks `entry.state === 'offered' && isExpired(entry, at)`.
  - Impact: Because `next.state` is `'accepted'`, `isLapsing(next, at)` always evaluates to `false`, so calling `acceptOffer` when `now() >= entry.expiresAt` succeeds and saves the expired offer as `accepted` instead of rejecting it.
  - Fix: Check `if (isLapsing(entry, at))` (or check `isExpired(entry, at)` after verifying `entry.state === 'offered'`) on the input `entry` before calling `moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at)` in `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`.

finding:
- `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:53-69`, `src/reservations/policy.mjs:5`: `rescheduleReservation` does not enforce the 240-minute maximum duration on the snapped reschedule window.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:21,197`): "A snapped window lasts at most 240 minutes." and "The new window must have an `endAt` value later than its `startAt` value. It is then snapped, and the snapped window must satisfy the duration limit and be available."
  - Implementation evidence: In `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:56-57`, `rescheduleReservation` computes `const window = {roomId: reservation.roomId, ...snapWindow({startAt, endAt})};` and checks `isRoomAvailable(...)`, then transitions, reprices, and saves the rescheduled hold without calling `exceedsMaxDuration(window)` (`src/reservations/policy.mjs:5`).
  - Impact: Calling `rescheduleReservation` with a new window whose snapped span exceeds 240 minutes (for example, 300 minutes) succeeds and persists an overlong reservation instead of rejecting the reschedule.
  - Fix: Check `if (exceedsMaxDuration(window)) throw new Error('reservation is too long');` in `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs` immediately after computing the snapped `window` and before mutating or saving state.

intentRequest rebuilds the request from a fixed list of invoice fields that leaves out issuedAt, so newIntent, which computes the fee with lateFee(prepared.total, prepared.issuedAt, at), gets a due instant of NaN and an intent created while its invoice is late has a fee of 0 and an amount equal to the total.

hasEnded compares minutesBetween(at, endAt), whole minutes truncated toward zero, with 0, so a closure with less than one minute left (for example 30 seconds) counts as ended: adding it is rejected and it is left out of the upcoming closures.

The single withdraw rule for waiting and offered entries carries the 60-minute cutoff, so a waiting entry whose startAt is less than 60 minutes from now cannot be withdrawn, although the limit applies only to offered entries.

ENTRY_DEFAULTS gives active: true and prepareRoom spreads it under the room entry, so a room entry without an active value becomes active and is selected for the report, although only rooms whose active value is true may be.
A credit reason is trimmed instead of being stored exactly as supplied.

newIntent passes PAYMENT_TERMS.authorizationHold, which is already minutes(10080) in milliseconds, to addMinutes, which multiplies by a minute again, so a new authorization expires 604,800,000 minutes later instead of 10080 minutes: an old authorization keeps blocking new intents for its invoice and can still be captured long after it should have expired.

paymentStatus passes the invoice record current to netPaid as its invoiceId argument; netPaid compares each intent's invoiceId (a string) with it using ===, and a string never equals an object, so no intent matches and the status reports paid 0 even after an intent of the invoice was captured.

AUDIT_LIMITS.maxQueryWindow is minutes(10080), a number of milliseconds, but prepareQuery compares it with windowSpan(query), which counts minutes ((until - from) / MINUTE), so the 10080-minute limit never triggers and longer query windows are accepted.

releaseTime rounds now() up to a whole minute with minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1) and then adds wait, but wait is counted from the local minute of day, which localMinuteOfDay takes from the start of the current minute; when now() is not on a minute boundary the result is one minute late (22:59:30 local with endMinute 23:00 gives 23:01 instead of 23:00), so releaseAt is not the first minute boundary after now() whose local minute is endMinute.

formatList writes each item through formatText, so a list item that starts with =, +, - or @ gets the ' prefix (for example the list ['-a', 'b'] is written '-a;b), although only text values get that prefix and a list's items are written as stored.

acceptOffer checks expiry with isLapsing(next, at), where next is the record returned by the accept transition, whose state is already accepted, while isLapsing is true only for an offered entry; so the check never fires and an expired offer can be accepted.

finding:
- `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7,9,23-28`, `src/exports/export-service.mjs:9,13,15-20,22-30`: `quoteField` uses a non-global regular expression when escaping double quotes, doubling only the first double quote in a quoted CSV field.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:241`): "A field containing a comma, double quote, carriage return or line feed is wrapped in double quotes, with inner double quotes doubled; other fields are written unchanged."
  - Implementation evidence: In `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7`, `quoteField` returns `` `"${text.replace(/"/, '""')}"` `` when `NEEDS_QUOTES.test(text)` is true, and `formatLine` / `buildCsv` (`src/exports/csv-format.mjs:9,23-28`) use `quoteField` for every header and row cell.
  - Impact: When any exported field or header contains two or more `"` characters (for example, `'say "hi" now'`), only the first `"` is doubled (`'"say ""hi" now"'` instead of `'"say ""hi"" now"'`), producing malformed CSV output across `exportRecords`, `exportRooms`, `exportHistory`, and `exportReservations`.
  - Fix: Replace `text.replace(/"/, '""')` in `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7` with `text.replaceAll('"', '""')` (or `text.replace(/"/g, '""')`).

finding:
- `src/exports/value-format.mjs:5,7-10,27-30`, `src/exports/reservation-columns.mjs:29`, `src/exports/export-service.mjs:9,13`: `formatList` applies `text` formula-prefix escaping to individual list items instead of writing list items as stored.
  - Governing requirement (`governing-spec.md:242-243`): "A `text` value must be a string and is written as stored, but with `'` prefixed when it starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`." and "a `list` of strings is joined with `;`, its items written as stored."
  - Implementation evidence: `formatList` in `src/exports/value-format.mjs:27-30` formats a `list` value via `value.map(formatText).join(';')`, where `formatText` (`src/exports/value-format.mjs:5,7-10`) prepends `'` whenever a string matches `/^[=+\-@]/`. `ROOM_COLUMNS` defines `amenities` as `kind: 'list'` (`src/exports/reservation-columns.mjs:29`), used by `exportRooms` (`src/exports/export-service.mjs:13`) and `exportRecords` (`src/exports/export-service.mjs:9`).
  - Impact: A `list` containing items starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` (for example, `['wifi', '+phone']` or `['-av']`) is written as `"wifi;'+phone"` or `"'-av"` with `'` injected before each matching item instead of writing the items as stored (`"wifi;+phone"` or `"-av"`).
  - Fix: Change `src/exports/value-format.mjs:29` from `return value.map(formatText).join(';');` to `return value.join(';');`.
